questions.text: What smell instantly drops you back into a specific year of your life? Describe where it takes you.
What did you use the internet for on the very first day you had it?
What meal did someone make for you as a kid that you've never been able to recreate?
What object from your childhood do you wish you still had, and what happened to it?
What did an entire summer day look like for you as a kid, hour by hour?
What was your first phone, and what's the one thing it did better than your current one?
What was on TV when you got home from school, and did you watch it or was it just noise?
Name a snack or drink that was everywhere back then and has completely vanished.
What piece of technology do you miss the physical feel of — the click, the weight, the sound it made?
What were you irrationally afraid of as a kid, and do you know where it came from?
Where did the kids in your area hang out that adults never went?
What was the first album, tape, or CD you owned, and were you proud of it or hiding it?
Describe the family car of your childhood — smell, sound, the seat you always got stuck with.
Which theme tune can you still sing every word of, unprompted, right now?
What was the best and worst thing about school lunches where you grew up?
What film did you watch so many times the tape or disc gave out?
Do you remember how you met your first proper friend? Are you still in touch?
What's your strongest memory of slow internet — waiting for something that would now take a second?
What household rule did you think was unreasonable as a kid and completely understand now?
What toy, collectible, or trading card were you completely obsessed with, and how deep did the collection get?
What's your clearest memory from a family trip, good or catastrophic?
Describe a grandparent's or relative's house from memory. What was always on the counter?
What's the school trip everyone in your year still talks about?
What song takes you straight back to being fifteen, for better or worse?
What were you not allowed to watch, play, or listen to — and did you find a way anyway?
Did you pass notes, sign yearbooks, or write letters? What's the one you'd want to read again?
What was the ritual of picking something to watch before streaming existed?
How did you get money as a kid, and what did you blow it on immediately?
Was there one family computer or console? How were the negotiations handled?
Who's someone you lost touch with completely and still wonder about?
What's the birthday party you remember best, yours or someone else's?
What's gone from your hometown that you'd bring back if you could?
What was the first thing you did that made you feel genuinely independent?
What was the first online community you were part of, and what happened to it?
What phase did you go through that your family will never let you live down?
What was on your bedroom walls as a teenager? Be specific and accept the consequences.
What slang did you and your friends use that nobody would understand now?
How did you get music before you could just search for it? Radio, burned discs, borrowed players?
What was the first thing you learned to cook by yourself, and how did the first attempt go?
What's a photo you wish existed of a moment nobody thought to capture?
Which class did you genuinely look forward to, and was it the subject or the teacher?
What was the ongoing conflict between you and a sibling or cousin, and who actually won?
What's the best costume you ever had as a kid, homemade or otherwise?
What hobby did you love as a kid and drop completely? Would you go back to it?
